note: Observed defensive blocks from NetTruder testing. Each entry is a test vector that was refused by an endpoint control or by a NetTruder guardrail. A block is a positive control result, not a coverage pass: it says nothing about the variants that were not attempted. None of these tests was bypassed.

kinds.endpoint-av: An endpoint security product refused the process or its content.
kinds.policy: An operating-system or enterprise policy refused the action.
kinds.guardrail: NetTruder refused its own action because a privilege or target-safety rule was not met.

blocks.product: McAfee endpoint, registered alongside Windows Defender
blocks.vector: HTA script host launches PowerShell directly
blocks.result: Blocked before process start; no engine events were produced.
blocks.scope: Parent-sensitive. The same command from cscript succeeded, so the path and arguments were valid. The control keyed on the mshta parent plus the child command line, not on powershell.exe alone.
blocks.valid: The endpoint control refused a script host starting a shell, which is the behaviour the mshta technique depends on. A refusal here is the control working, not a broken test.
blocks.teaches: Test proxy execution as a parent/child chain, not as a standalone binary. A valid Microsoft signature on mshta.exe does not mean the child process will be allowed.
blocks.detect: 4688 or Sysmon 1 where ParentImage ends in mshta.exe and Image ends in powershell.exe or cmd.exe. Alert on the chain, not only on the child command line.
blocks.followup: Keep the allowed control (cmd /c echo hi) in the test matrix so a block is never confused with a broken harness. Add the mshta-to-shell chain to the ASR and parent-image guidance.
blocks.evidence: RESEARCH.md section 4. The allow/deny matrix was run on 2026-11-13 and recorded in the read-out; the error code was read from the Wsh.Run HRESULT.

blocks.product: McAfee endpoint, registered alongside Windows Defender
blocks.result: Refused at process start. No download completed and no egress alert was raised because the process never reached the network.
blocks.signal: McAfee notification: file contains a virus or potentially unwanted software
blocks.scope: The command shape is exact; the original URL and temp path were not retained in a machine log, so this is a documented test vector rather than a byte-for-byte replay.
blocks.valid: The endpoint control refused a signed system binary using the documented download arguments before it could touch the network. That is exactly the outcome a download-control test is meant to observe.
blocks.teaches: AV content and behaviour rules can cover a LOLBAS vector before the network layer does. A missing EGRESS_CERTUTIL alert is not an IDS miss when the process was never created; check the endpoint product log before calling it a gap.
blocks.detect: certutil with -urlcache, -split, -verifyctl, -decode, -encode or a URL. Correlate with endpoint product events 1116/1117 (Defender) or the McAfee event log, and with 4688/Sysmon 1 if available.
blocks.followup: Record the endpoint verdict alongside the IDS verdict. Add a report line that separates 'blocked before execution' from 'executed but not observed'.

variants.result: blocked by McAfee at process start
not tested - normal certificate use, outside the download test

blocks.evidence: RESEARCH.md section 10.4. Recorded as prose during the egress test; no machine log captured the argv or the McAfee event id.

blocks.vector: Block a public address without elevation
blocks.result: Refused. The console reported that an elevated session is required and created zero firewall rules.
blocks.signal: Elevation check failed before New-NetFirewallRule was called.
blocks.scope: Also enforced in code: local address, gateway, DNS server, loopback, multicast, broadcast and reserved ranges are refused, and private peers need explicit confirmation.
blocks.valid: A network containment tool must not be able to cut off its own management path or a public service without authority. Refusing is the safer and correct behaviour.
blocks.teaches: Not every blocked command is an AV result. Separate product blocks, policy blocks and self-guardrails in the report so an operator knows which control acted.
blocks.detect: Audit entry for the refused block attempt, plus the console message. No firewall rule should exist afterwards.
blocks.followup: Add an audit assertion to the test plan: after a refused block, NetTruder-IPS-* rule count must still be zero.
